'''J Paul Luzio''' <small>[[FMedSci]]</small> (born 15 August 1947)<ref name="whoswho">[http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U2000230 LUZIO, Prof. (John) Paul], ''Who's Who 2014'', A & C Black, 2014; online edn, Oxford University Press, 2014</ref> is a British biologist who is Professor of [[Molecular Membrane Biology]], Department of Clinical Biochemistry at the [[University of Cambridge]], and was Master of [[St Edmund's College, Cambridge]] until 2014, as well as Director of the [[Cambridge Bio-Medical Campus#The Cambridge Institute for Medical Research|Cambridge Institute for Medical Research]].

He was a student at [[Clare College, Cambridge]]<ref name="whoswho"/> reading Natural Sciences (Part II [[Biochemistry]]) as an undergraduate and studying for a Ph.D. in the Department of Biochemistry. After a period in [[Cardiff]] as a lecturer of medical biochemistry at the [[Welsh National School of Medicine]], he returned to Cambridge where he became a lecturer in clinical biochemistry. He was subsequently promoted to Reader and then Professor.

Luzio's research is largely concerned with [[Intracellular membranes|intracellular membrane]] traffic pathways in mammalian cells and his research group is funded by a programme grant from the [[Medical Research Council (UK)|Medical Research Council]] and project grant support from the [[Wellcome Trust]].

He is an Honorary Fellow of [[St Edmund's College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.st-edmunds.cam.ac.uk/people/professor-paul-luzio|title=St Edmund's College - University of Cambridge|website=www.st-edmunds.cam.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-09-10}}</ref>
